content: Succinylsulfathiazole, also spelled as succinylsulphathiazole, is a sulfonamide compound. It appears as a white or yellowish-white crystalline powder. This substance is soluble in aqueous solutions of alkali hydroxides and carbonates but exhibits very limited solubility in water. Pharmacologically, it is categorized as an ultra-long-acting drug. Approximately 95% of the drug remains localized in the intestine, while only about 5% undergoes slow hydrolysis to sulfathiazole, which is then absorbed systemically. The primary therapeutic application of succinylsulfathiazole is its antibacterial activity within the gastrointestinal tract (GIT). The recommended dosage ranges from 10 grams to 20 grams per day, administered in divided doses.
